# Zerro

> Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar utility that turns a screen recording and spoken instructions into a structured prompt for AI coding agents. Frame a region of your screen, dictate what you want, and Zerro returns a Markdown prompt ready to paste into Cursor, Windsurf, v0, or any agent. Audio isolation and frame downsampling always happen on your Mac first; the AI step runs in the cloud on the Managed plan, or — with BYOK — goes straight to the provider on your own key, no Zerro servers in the middle and no account required.

Zerro is built for developers who already work with AI coding agents and would rather talk through a change than type out every instruction. You speak roughly 4× faster than you type; Zerro closes that gap by capturing what's on screen alongside what you say.

## How it works

- Hit the hotkey and drag to frame the part of your screen the agent should see.
- Dictate what you want in plain language — up to 3 minutes per recording.
- Zerro isolates the audio and downsamples the frames locally, then makes a single API call.
- A structured Markdown prompt lands on your clipboard, ready to paste into your agent.

## Key facts

- Platform: native macOS app (Swift & SwiftUI, built on ScreenCaptureKit). Not Electron.
- Processing: local-first — audio isolation and frame downsampling happen on your machine.
- Keys: bring your own OpenAI and Gemini keys, stored in the macOS Keychain.
- Recording cap: 3 minutes per recording, for fast and predictable cost.
- Distribution: signed & notarized .dmg, with Sparkle auto-updates.
- Pricing: BYOK is $39 one-time (available now). A Managed plan at $12/month is coming soon.
